content_html:
The right washer cycle depends more on fabric, soil level, and load size than on the marketing name printed on the dial. Start with the care label of the most delicate item, separate incompatible loads, and use the gentlest cycle that achieves the result. Longer, hotter, or faster-spinning is not automatically better.

Start with the most delicate care label

If one item calls for a delicate cycle or cold water, that limit should govern a mixed load. Separate heavy towels, jeans, and zippered items from fine fabrics when friction or weight could damage them.

Use normal for durable everyday loads

Durable cottons and everyday blends usually do well on a normal cycle when labels allow it. Choose temperature for color, soil, and care guidance; do not increase heat simply because a load looks dirty.

Use delicate or permanent-press settings for gentler handling

Delicate settings usually reduce agitation and/or spin, while permanent press may moderate mechanical action and wrinkling. Names vary by manufacturer, so check what each cycle actually changes on your machine.

A bulky cycle does not fix overloading

Comforters and large items need room to move and sometimes a higher-capacity machine. If an item fills the drum dry and cannot redistribute, a special cycle does not guarantee proper washing or spinning.
